title: He said that...
goal: Student reports what someone said using correct backshift of tenses, pronouns, time and place references.
connects_to: M18 (Reported questions + commands) — extends to interrogatives and imperatives.
module_chunks: He said he was tired (present → past)
She said she had finished (past → past perfect)
He said he would call (will → would)
He said he could come (can → could)
He said it that day (today → that day)
He said he lived there (here → there)
He mentioned that... / He explained that... / He claimed that...

units.title: He said that
units.grammar_focus: Reported speech with say/tell + backshift present → past
units.real_life_context: You report someone's statement, shifting present to past as time passes.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I am tired." Reported: "He said he _____ tired."
grammar.explanation: Reported speech: present simple ("am tired") shifts to past simple ("was tired") when the reporting verb is in the past ("said"). Basic backshift.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I work in finance." Reported: "She said she _____ in finance."
grammar.explanation: Present simple → past simple in reported speech. "Works" becomes "worked".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I'm cooking dinner." Reported: "He said he _____ dinner."
grammar.explanation: Present continuous ("am cooking") → past continuous ("was cooking") in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I like coffee." Reported: "She said she _____ coffee."
grammar.explanation: Present simple → past simple. "Likes" becomes "liked".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "We live in São Paulo." Reported: "They said they _____ in São Paulo."
grammar.explanation: "Live" (present) → "lived" (past) in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I am studying English." Reported: "He said he _____ English."
grammar.explanation: "Am studying" (present continuous) → "was studying" (past continuous) in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I don't understand." Reported: "She said she _____ understand."
grammar.explanation: "Don't / Do not" (present) → "didn't / did not" (past) in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I'm tired." Reported: "He said that he is tired."
grammar.answer: He said that he was tired.
grammar.explanation: Reported speech after "said" requires backshift: "is" becomes "was". Keeping "is" is a common mistake.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I like pizza." Reported: "She said she like pizza."
grammar.explanation: Two fixes needed: backshift to "liked" and 3rd person singular. "She liked" — past simple.

grammar.passage: He said he was tired. She said she worked in finance. They said they lived in São Paulo. He said he was studying English.
grammar.question: What did she say she did for work?
grammar.explanation: The text says "She said she worked in finance".

listening_speaking.text: He said he was tired.
She said she worked in finance.
They said they lived in São Paulo.
He said he was cooking dinner.
She said she didn't understand.

units.title: She told me
units.grammar_focus: Reported speech: difference between "say" and "tell" (tell requires object)
units.real_life_context: You choose between "say" (no object) and "tell" (always with object) when reporting.

grammar.sentence: She _____ me that she was tired.
grammar.explanation: "Tell + person" — requires a direct object. "Told me" = to me. "Said" wouldn't take "me" without "to" ("said to me"). "Tell" is more natural.

grammar.sentence: He _____ that the meeting was canceled.
grammar.explanation: "Said + that-clause" with no object. "He said that..." — not "he told that". "Tell" would need a person.

grammar.sentence: She _____ her sister the news.
grammar.explanation: "Tell + person + thing" — natural chunk. "Told her sister the news".

grammar.sentence: He _____ to me about the project.
grammar.explanation: "Spoke to me" — preposition "to" with "speak". Another way to report a conversation.

grammar.sentence: She _____ me she was going on vacation.
grammar.explanation: "Told me + that-clause" — the verb "tell" always requires a person.

grammar.sentence: He _____ that he didn't want to come.
grammar.explanation: "Said that" — the verb "say" doesn't take a direct object before the that-clause.

grammar.sentence: She _____ the children a story.
grammar.explanation: "Told the children a story" — natural structure with tell.

grammar.sentence: She said me that she was tired.
grammar.answer: She told me that she was tired.
grammar.explanation: "Say" doesn't take a direct object without "to". "Said to me" would work, but "told me" is more natural.

grammar.sentence: He told that the meeting was canceled.
grammar.answer: He said that the meeting was canceled.
grammar.explanation: "Tell" without an object doesn't work. Either use "said" (no person), or add a person ("told someone, told everyone").

grammar.passage: She told me that she was tired. He said that the meeting was canceled. She told her sister the news. He spoke to me about the project last week.
grammar.question: Who did she tell about being tired?
grammar.explanation: The text says "She told me that she was tired".

listening_speaking.text: She told me she was tired.
He said that the meeting was canceled.
She told her sister the news.
He spoke to me about it.
She mentioned that she was leaving.

units.title: She said she had
units.grammar_focus: Reported speech backshift: past → past perfect; present perfect → past perfect
units.real_life_context: You report past actions someone described, shifting tenses one step back.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I finished the report." Reported: "He said he _____ the report."
grammar.explanation: Past simple ("finished") → past perfect ("had finished") in reported speech. One more step back in time.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I have visited Paris." Reported: "She said she _____ Paris."
grammar.explanation: Present perfect ("have visited") → past perfect ("had visited") in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I saw the movie." Reported: "He said he _____ the movie."
grammar.explanation: Past simple → past perfect. "Saw" → "had seen". Standard backshift.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I've been to Japan." Reported: "She said she _____ to Japan."
grammar.explanation: "Have been" → "had been" in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I lost my phone." Reported: "He said he _____ his phone."
grammar.explanation: "Lost" → "had lost". Past simple to past perfect.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I've finished the project." Reported: "She said she _____ the project."
grammar.explanation: "Have finished" → "had finished" in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I read that book." Reported: "He said he _____ that book."
grammar.explanation: "Read" (past) → "had read" (past perfect). Note: pronounced /red/ in both.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I finished it." Reported: "He said he finished it."
grammar.hint: Past simple precisa ir para past perfect
grammar.answer: He said he had finished it.
grammar.explanation: In reported speech, "finished" must become "had finished". One more step back in time.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I've seen the movie." Reported: "She said she has seen the movie."
grammar.answer: She said she had seen the movie.
grammar.explanation: "Has seen" in reported speech becomes "had seen". Backshift is required.

grammar.passage: He said he had finished the report. She said she had visited Paris twice. He said he had seen the movie three times. They said they had been to Japan for vacation.
grammar.question: How many times had he seen the movie?
grammar.explanation: The text says "He said he had seen the movie three times".

listening_speaking.text: He said he had finished it.
She said she had been to Paris.
They said they had lost the keys.
He said he had seen the movie.
She said she had already eaten.

units.title: He said he would
units.grammar_focus: Reported speech backshift for modals: will → would, can → could, may → might, must → had to
units.real_life_context: You report promises, possibilities, abilities, and obligations someone mentioned.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I will call you." Reported: "He said he _____ call me."
grammar.explanation: "Will" → "would" no reported speech. "Said he would call" — promessa reportada.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I can swim." Reported: "She said she _____ swim."
grammar.explanation: "Can" → "could" no reported. "Said she could swim".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I may be late." Reported: "He said he _____ be late."
grammar.explanation: "May" → "might" em reported speech. "Might be late".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I must leave." Reported: "She said she _____ leave."
grammar.explanation: "Must" → "had to" em reported speech. "Said she had to leave".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I won't be there." Reported: "He said he _____ be there."
grammar.explanation: "Won't / Will not" (will not) → "wouldn't / would not" (would not) em reported.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I can't do it." Reported: "She said she _____ do it."
grammar.explanation: "Can't / Cannot" → "couldn't / could not" em reported. Backshift padrão.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I'll send the email." Reported: "He said he _____ send the email."
grammar.explanation: "Will send" → "would send" in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I will help." Reported: "He said he will help."
grammar.explanation: Backshift is required: "will" → "would" when the reporting verb is in the past.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I must work tomorrow." Reported: "She said she must work the next day."
grammar.answer: She said she had to work the next day.
grammar.explanation: "Must" stays unchanged in some modern contexts, but in traditional reported speech → "had to".

grammar.passage: He said he would call me later. She said she could speak three languages. He said he might be late for dinner. She said she had to leave early.
grammar.question: Why might he be late?
accepts: he might be late for dinner
grammar.explanation: The text says "He said he might be late for dinner".

listening_speaking.text: He said he would call me.
She said she could swim.
He said he might be late.
She said she had to leave.
He said he wouldn't come.

units.title: Time and place shifts
units.grammar_focus: Time/place changes in reported speech (today → that day, here → there, this → that, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before)
units.real_life_context: You report with full natural shifts of time/place references — mature reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I'm tired today." Reported: "He said he was tired _____."
grammar.explanation: "Today" becomes "that day" in reported speech — when reporting after the fact. Natural time shift.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I'll come tomorrow." Reported: "She said she would come _____."
grammar.explanation: "Tomorrow" → "the next day" (or "the following day") in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I was here yesterday." Reported: "He said he had been _____ the day before."
grammar.explanation: "Here" → "there" in reported speech (you're no longer at the original place).

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I saw it yesterday." Reported: "She said she had seen it _____."
grammar.explanation: "Yesterday" → "the day before" (or "the previous day") in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I love this song." Reported: "He said he loved _____ song."
grammar.explanation: "This" → "that" in reported speech — you're more distant from the referent.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I'll call you next week." Reported: "She said she would call me the _____ week."
grammar.explanation: "Next week" → "the following week" in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I came here last year." Reported: "He said he had come _____ the year before."
grammar.explanation: "Here" → "there" + "last year" → "the year before".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I work here." Reported: "He said he worked here."
grammar.hint: "Here" precisa mudar — você não está no mesmo lugar
grammar.explanation: "Here" stays only if you're still in the same place. For distant reporting, use "there".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I'll see you tomorrow." Reported: "She said she would see me tomorrow."
grammar.answer: She said she would see me the next day.
grammar.explanation: "Tomorrow" stays only if the report is still today. Otherwise, "the next day".

grammar.passage: He said he was tired that day. She said she would come the next day. He said he had been there the day before. She said she loved that song.
grammar.question: When did she say she would come?
grammar.explanation: The text says "She said she would come the next day".

listening_speaking.text: He said he was tired that day.
She said she would come the next day.
He said he had been there.
She said she loved that song.
He mentioned he had seen it the day before.

cross_unit_consolidation: Backshift: present → past, past → past perfect, will → would, can → could, may → might, must → had to
Mudanças de tempo: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, now → then
Mudanças de pronome: I → he/she, you → I/me, we → they
Mudanças de demonstrativo: this → that, these → those
Reporting verbs alternativos: mentioned, explained, claimed, stated
